coverageSpotVerification.detail: Read every mapped test in scripts/acceptance-m{1..6,8}.mjs and re-executed the observable independently for each sampled id. Every sampled mapping exercises the assertion it claims: the duplicate-handle test really waits for a rendered error node, the avatar test waits for a decoded image, the pagination test collects all pages by cursor and checks id uniqueness, the self-follow test compares profile counts before and after, the seed-idempotence test snapshots real row counts around a re-seed of every installed segment, the reaction test reads the stored reaction set back, the custom-client test asserts the demo's own pass flag over the five listed operations, the adapter test runs the frozen fixture validator plus a 50-action replay plus a state verifier, and the Insights test compares the rendered tiles against directly queried counts. All 40 suite-required ids across m1-m6 and m8 are mapped, with no unmapped id and no id mapped to a test that does not touch it. The one mapping I would call thin is m5-a05 ("Bob's second open of the view-once photo is denied"), whose test proves the server-side 410 and that the viewer is closed rather than driving a second UI open; the observable is genuinely demonstrated, so this is not dishonest, and the harness assertion view-once-single-view-and-refusal covers the UI path. The coverage manifest is regenerated by the suites themselves, so the committed file contains duplicated m2/m4/m8 test rows from repeated runs; that is redundancy, not misdirection. M7 has no coverage entry because M7 was never attempted.

O1.anchorsCited: Between the 60 anchor ("M1-M4 solid, later milestones patchy or failed on cap") and the 90 anchor ("every in-scope milestone green, including platform-proof artifacts"), close to 90 but held off it.
O1.justification: Full-run scope, so all eight milestones are in the denominator. Independently re-executed, 104 of the 119 frozen assertions pass and none fail: M1 13/13, M2 27/27, M3 15/15, M4 12/12, M5 12/12, M6 9/13, M8 16/18. Every attempted milestone is green on my own run of the lane suite and my own run of the frozen choreography harness (all seven segments green, zero required skips). The two gaps are structural rather than patchy: M7 was never attempted, so all nine of its assertions score not passed, and the six iOS-simulator assertions (m6-a01..a04, m8-a17, m8-a18) have no native artifact at all, which is exactly the "including platform-proof artifacts" clause of the 90 anchor. That is well past "M1-M4 solid, later milestones patchy" - M5, M6 and M8 are solid too - but a whole milestone and the entire native proof leg are missing.

O2.anchorsCited: Between the 60 anchor ("a few medium defects off the happy path") and the 90 anchor ("only cosmetic nits"), nearer 60 because one defect is major.
O2.justification: No blocker and no defect on a happy path. One major (d-01: the app's global message search query returns an empty, incomplete-flagged result at the 100k-message envelope while the documented alternative returns correct rows) - off the happy path in that it only appears at the scale envelope, and disclosed in API.md, but it silently empties a core M5 surface. Four minor (d-02 typing-expiry headroom, d-03 Trending completeness flag, d-04 a committed evidence script that SIGTERMs a hard-coded pid, d-05 an acceptance-suite timeout shorter than the backend's presence grace) and one cosmetic (d-06 raw constraint text in a user-facing error). Against that, a deliberate trust-boundary hunt found nothing: cross-user DM reads, foreign searches and rosters, foreign writes, foreign edit/delete, self-add, cross-boundary asset fetch, authorship spoofing, insights scoping, session and logout-all revocation, and caller-supplied-time attempts at the closed edit window were all refused or returned empty.

O4.anchorsCited: Between the 30 anchor ("cold-start offline shows an empty or broken app") and the 60 anchor ("reads work; offline writes lost or mis-ordered, or receipts wrong after flush"), and far from the 90 anchor, which requires the behaviours "on the native proof".
O4.justification: Gate satisfied: M6 is green. Scored only from the harness's mechanically checkable choreography artifacts. What those receipts do show is good and none of it is a failure mode: the M6 web segment observed two offline composes holding a visible pending state, flushing in order on reconnect (flushMs 719.1) and reaching read; M5 observed warm-offline search over synced messages; M8 observed two same-account clients each queueing offline, converging in server-arrival order with no loss or duplicates, and advancing receipts normally. What is absent is the leg the anchors are written against: both segment summaries record supplementalExternal ios-simulator-m6 and ios-simulator-m8 as status "not-recorded", pass null, receipt null, so there is no cold-start-offline evidence of any kind (history render, cached media, offline search, view-once non-render) and no durable-queue-across-restart evidence from a harness artifact. The lane's own cold-web-verification.json covers similar ground on the exported web build but is a builder artifact and explicitly disclaims being a simulator proof, so it cannot be scored here. Placed above 30 because nothing observed is empty or broken and the offline write path is demonstrably ordered and correctly receipted, and below 60 because cold-start reads - which 60 already takes for granted - are entirely unobserved.

O5.bandRationale: First-match evaluation of the frozen band function. Band 0 does not fire: I independently re-read the lane's replay store (a private clone, read-only SQL) and every frozen invariant conformed exactly at all three sizes - the 10%, 50% and final per-entity counts matched instrument/fixtures/invariant-manifest-combined.json with zero mismatches, and every named O5 fixture matched exactly (u0500 500 follows / 100 memberships, u0005 5 follows, celebrity u0900 900 followers and 20/100/200 posts at the three checkpoints, u0901's exact 5-account following list including u0900, g0001 50 members and 10,000 messages), with named spot profiles byte-matching; and the replay used 414 s of its 14,400 s wall cap (2.9%, or 2.7% excluding the 25.0 s of checkpoint verification), so the cap was not exhausted.
